name: DX Hunter
description: DX Hunter is designed to make HF band operation faster and more organized. When you find activity on a frequency, mark it instantly, continue scanning the band, and jump back to your stored frequencies whenever you want — without having to remember or write them down.

features.title: Mark frequencies instantly
features.description: Found an active or interesting frequency? Mark it immediately and continue searching the band. No need to write frequencies down or try to remember them.

features.title: Navigate between marked frequencies
features.description: Use the TO DO buttons or the mouse wheel on the marker side of the vertical axis. Navigation stays within the current band, visits only pending TO DO frequencies, and restores each saved operating mode. Use the wheel on the blue side for direct tuning. Wheel up increases frequency; wheel down decreases it.

features.title: TO DO / TO SKIP / QSO DONE
features.description: The blue tuning cursor sits to the left of the vertical frequency scale. Green QSO DONE, yellow TO DO and red TO SKIP markers align with their exact frequencies on the right. Click a contact row to tune to the saved frequency and mode.

features.title: ADIF export
features.description: Generate an ADIF log file from your completed QSOs for easy import into QRZ.com and other logging software that supports the ADIF standard.

features.title: Cabrillo export for contests
features.description: Export completed contacts with sent and received exchanges. A contest name is required; check the exported format against your contest rules.

features.title: Direct DSP control
features.description: Adjust DNR, SHIFT and WIDTH directly from the computer interface while operating, without navigating through radio menus.

features.title: Multiple QSOs on one frequency
features.description: Log different stations on the same frequency without overwriting previous contacts. Press TO DO to prepare the next contact. The RADIO list keeps worked contacts and pending stations in separate rows.

features.title: Live contest duplicate warnings
features.description: In Contest Mode, a possible duplicate warning appears while typing a callsign already worked on the same band in the current contest. You can still confirm the contact when contest rules permit it. Checks do not save or refresh the log on every keystroke.

features.title: Configurable contest exchanges
features.description: Record sent and received exchanges. Configure a fixed exchange, automatic serial numbering, or a combination such as {serial} SC . Contest mode requires a callsign, both RSTs and both exchanges before confirming a contact. Outside contest mode, exchange fields and labels are disabled and serial numbers are not incremented. INFO settings apply when leaving the tab.

features.title: Confirmed contacts at a glance
features.description: The LOG tab lists every contact independently, including multiple contacts on the same frequency. Review UTC date/time, callsign, exact frequency, mode, RSTs, exchanges and comments. Sort columns or delete one selected QSO without removing other contacts at that frequency. Double-click a contact's UTC date/time to edit it; validated changes are saved automatically and included in exports.

features.title: Automatic QSO recovery
features.description: All completed contacts, frequency markers, pending contact details and the next serial number are recovered on startup. Existing recovery files migrate automatically to version 1.0.1's format. No log export is required before closing.

features.title: Connect your way
features.description: CONNECT/DISCONNECT is in the SERIAL tab. Enable “Connect automatically on startup” to connect with your saved settings. The display shows DISCONNECTED while disconnected. The radio connection closes automatically when you exit.

features.title: Quick signal reports
features.description: Set sent and received RSTs to 59 with separate buttons beside each field. A callsign and both reports are required for every confirmed QSO; contest mode also requires both exchanges.

features.title: Smoother keyboard entry
features.description: TAB and Shift+TAB skip action buttons, and the read-only QSO date/time field does not receive focus. Edits are applied when a field loses focus, including when switching tabs, except where an explicit SAVE button is provided. CALLSIGN, COMMENTS, MY CALLSIGN and both exchange fields use uppercase text. Tab titles also stay out of the keyboard focus sequence. Editable contact fields have a lighter background so they are easy to identify.

features.title: Contact comments
features.description: Add notes about a station or contact using the COMMENTS field beside CALLSIGN.

features.title: Version and project information
features.description: The ABOUT tab shows the installed version, the author and clickable links to email, the website, GitHub and releases.

features.title: Local and UTC clocks
features.description: Live clocks above the control panel show the PC's local time above UTC, with both updated every second.

features.title: VFO A frequency
features.description: Monitor the current VFO A frequency in real time and change frequency directly from DX Hunter.

features.title: Operating modes
features.description: Select LSB, USB, CW, FM and AM directly from the interface.

features.title: DNR, SHIFT and WIDTH
features.description: Frequently adjusted DSP controls remain immediately accessible while you operate and move between stations.

features.title: Save and resume QSO sessions
features.description: SAVE SESSION stores completed contacts in a .dxh file for later use, including multi-day contests. LOAD SESSION restores the log and contest settings. NEW SESSION clears completed contacts. TO DO and TO SKIP markers remain independent and are preserved when loading or starting a session.

features.title: Band buttons with default modes
features.description: Select a band directly above the frequency display to restore its last frequency. Set a default mode for each band in BANDS and click SAVE BANDS. A mode saved at the target frequency takes priority over the band default. The mode is applied before the frequency.

features.title: Clear pending markers separately
features.description: UNMARK ALL in RADIO removes TO DO and TO SKIP markers while preserving completed contacts. LOG contains completed-contact management and ADIF/Cabrillo exports; INFO follows LOG.

features.title: Live TX meter history
features.description: The METERS tab, immediately after RADIO, shows 20-second histories for output power, SWR, ALC, drain current (ID) and speech compression (COMP). A two-reading moving average makes changes easier to follow. Reference scales estimate watts, SWR, amperes and dB; ALC stays relative. These estimates are not factory calibration.

features.title: More room to operate
features.description: The main window now opens at up to 1280 × 800, adapting to the available screen area. Meter sampling runs only while METERS is open and enabled, sharing the CAT queue with priority for normal radio controls.

features.title: Antenna profiles and RF power
features.description: Set RF power presets by transmit band in ANTENNAS. Choose the connected antenna in RADIO and use the RF POWER slider to adjust power in 10 W steps up to the preset.

features.title: QRZ lookup
features.description: Open a station's QRZ.com page from RADIO and record its No QRZ Logbook status with the contact.

steps: Find activity Tune normally across the band using your FTDX10.
Press TO DO Store the current frequency and operating mode immediately and continue searching.
Keep exploring Mark as many interesting frequencies as you find.
Jump between them Use the TO DO buttons or the mouse wheel on the marker side to revisit memories in the current band.
Complete the QSO Enter the callsign and both RST reports, then press QSO DONE. Other marked frequencies remain available for QSOs still to be made.
installation: Download the ZIP and extract dx-hunter.exe into a writable folder.
When upgrading, replace the executable and keep your existing settings and QSO recovery JSON files beside it.
Connect your FTDX10 by USB, with its USB serial driver installed.
Run dx-hunter.exe. In SERIAL, select your radio's CAT COM port and matching settings, then click CONNECT. Enable “Connect automatically on startup” if desired.

Use TO DO to store a frequency and mode or TO SKIP to mark a station to skip. Use the wheel on the blue side to tune and on the marker side to revisit TO DO stations in the current band. Enter CALLSIGN, RST S and RST R before QSO DONE.
For contests, enable Contest mode in INFO and configure your exchange and optional serial number. Both sent and received exchanges are then required. Settings apply when you leave INFO.
Review confirmed contacts in LOG and export ADIF or Cabrillo as needed.
To work another station on a frequency with completed QSOs, press TO DO. Existing contacts and their green marker remain in the log; complete the new contact with QSO DONE.

In LOG, double-click a completed contact's UTC date/time to edit it (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM). Use SAVE SESSION to archive completed contacts in a .dxh file, LOAD SESSION to resume them, and NEW SESSION to start an empty log. These session actions preserve TO DO and TO SKIP markers.

In BANDS, configure each band's frequency limits and default mode (LSB, USB, CW, FM or AM), then click SAVE BANDS. Band buttons restore the last frequency and use its saved mode when available, otherwise the band's default. UNMARK ALL in RADIO clears pending markers while retaining completed contacts.

Open METERS and enable TX meter history to view the five transmit histories. Sampling pauses when you leave the tab. Right-hand scales marked ≈ are estimates; compare them with the radio. ALC uses a relative 0–64 reference.
